text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambia press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police have arrested over 20 men in investigations into a racket in which Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines has allegedly been paying ghost workers.

- Acting secretary general of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) Erastus Mwencha, says the suspension of secretary general Bingu Wa Mutharika has had no effect on the regional groupings operations.
- The ruling Movement for Multi-party Democracy (MMD) has urged Western donors to ignore calls by former president Kenneth Kaunda to impose more aid cuts on Zambia.
- Stockborers in southern Zambia have destroyed about 100 hectares of maize crop, the agriculture minister said.
- Former president Kenneth Kaunda says he is still convinced new elections will be held this year after his party boycotted a national poll last year
